title: Rulers, Dynasties & Empires
summary: A curated selection of major world rulers, dynasties, and empires with reign span and realm.
source: Historical facts (dates are conventional and sometimes approximate/contested). A curated selection across civilizations, not exhaustive.

rows.name: Hammurabi
rows.note: Issued one of the earliest written law codes.

rows.name: Tutankhamun
rows.note: The 'boy king'; tomb found nearly intact in 1922.

rows.name: Ramesses II
rows.note: 'Ramesses the Great'; long reign and vast monuments.

rows.name: Cyrus the Great
rows.note: Founder; known for tolerance of conquered peoples.

rows.name: Darius I
rows.note: Organized the empire into satrapies; Royal Road.

rows.name: Alexander the Great
rows.note: Conquered from Greece to India; spread Hellenistic culture.

rows.name: Qin Shi Huang
rows.note: First emperor of a unified China; Terracotta Army.

rows.name: Ashoka
rows.note: Spread Buddhism after the Kalinga War.

rows.name: Cleopatra VII
rows.note: Last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt.

rows.name: Julius Caesar
rows.note: Crossed the Rubicon; assassinated on the Ides of March.

rows.name: Augustus
rows.note: First Roman emperor; began the Pax Romana.

rows.name: Constantine the Great
rows.note: Legalized Christianity; founded Constantinople.

rows.name: Wu Zetian
rows.note: The only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right.

rows.name: Justinian I
rows.note: Codified Roman law (Corpus Juris Civilis); built Hagia Sophia.

rows.name: Charlemagne
rows.note: Crowned 'Emperor of the Romans' in 800.

rows.name: Saladin
rows.note: Recaptured Jerusalem during the Crusades.

rows.name: Genghis Khan
rows.note: Founder of the largest contiguous land empire in history.

rows.name: Kublai Khan
rows.note: Founded the Yuan dynasty in China.

rows.name: Mansa Musa
rows.note: Famed for immense wealth and his pilgrimage to Mecca.

rows.name: Henry VIII
rows.note: Broke with Rome; founded the Church of England.

rows.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
rows.note: Ottoman peak in territory, law, and culture.

rows.name: Akbar
rows.note: Expanded the empire; known for religious tolerance.

rows.name: Elizabeth I
rows.note: Elizabethan era; defeat of the Spanish Armada (1588).

rows.name: Montezuma II
rows.note: Ruled at the time of the Spanish conquest.

rows.name: Louis XIV
rows.note: The 'Sun King'; absolute monarchy at Versailles.

rows.name: Peter the Great
rows.note: Modernized and westernized Russia; founded St. Petersburg.

rows.name: Catherine the Great
rows.note: Expanded Russia; era of enlightened absolutism.

rows.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
rows.note: Dominated Europe; the Napoleonic Code.

rows.name: Queen Victoria
rows.note: Victorian era; empire at vast extent.

rows.name: Roman Empire
rows.note: Eastern (Byzantine) half lasted until 1453.

rows.name: Han dynasty
rows.note: Golden age; the Silk Road flourished.

rows.name: Tang dynasty
rows.note: Cosmopolitan high point of Chinese culture.

rows.name: Ming dynasty
rows.note: Voyages of Zheng He; the Forbidden City.

rows.name: Qing dynasty
rows.note: China's last imperial dynasty.

rows.name: Byzantine Empire
rows.note: Capital Constantinople; fell to the Ottomans in 1453.

rows.name: Ottoman Empire
rows.note: Ended with the founding of the Republic of Turkey.
